clue.text: American writer putting a point to a hired killer

parts.note: W, for west, is one of the points of the compass
a hit man is a contract killer paid to murder

explanation.surface: Someone sharpens a hired assassin, or gives him a direction, in an odd literary scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' here is a compass point, not a sharp tip: W (west) is put before the hired killer.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt Whitman was the nineteenth-century poet of Leaves of Grass, a famous American author.

clue.text: Fish-press used to give the required firmness

definitions.text: used to give the required firmness

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line
to iron clothes is to press them flat

explanation.surface: A fish press is applied to make something properly firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish-press' looks like one gadget but splits into two verbs, fish and press.
explanation.definitionFit: This L-section metal bar is a structural member fitted to stiffen frames and brackets.

clue.text: A scientist must be up-to-date, not backward-looking

parts.note: something up-to-date is new

indicators.note: looking backward says the little word not is read from right to left

explanation.surface: A researcher should keep current and not look to the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton was the physicist behind the laws of motion and gravitation.

clue.text: A sale's on as arranged, but only for a limited period

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the phrase are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A shop sale is on, but it runs only for a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as arranged' rearranges A SALES ON, ignoring the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tied to a particular time of year lasts only for that stretch.

clue.text: Old actor getting lonely girl parts to play

indicators.note: play signals that the fifteen letters are moved about freely

explanation.surface: A veteran thespian gets cast as solitary young women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to play' rearranges all fifteen letters of LONELY GIRL PARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling troupes of performers went from town to town in earlier centuries, so this describes a historical actor.

clue.text: He must expect denunciation for lighting up

definitions.text: He must expect denunciation for lighting up

parts.words: He must expect denunciation for lighting up
parts.note: reads like a smoker being scolded, but the lighting up is setting fire to buildings deliberately

explanation.surface: A smoker should brace for disapproval when he lights a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-raiser who sets property ablaze on purpose would be condemned for it.

clue.text: A person having to admit royalty

parts.note: to own up is to admit, so own means admit
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone is made to own up to being of royal blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who possesses a thing has it, so a possessor is a person having.

clue.text: Colonial high-rise building

parts.note: seems to describe a tower block in a colony, but the colony is of insects and the mound they build

explanation.surface: A tall block erected in some overseas colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects living in colonies heap up a tall mound of earth as their home.

clue.text: Coppers maybe make a difference

definitions.meaning: copper coins are an example of loose coins in your pocket
to alter something is to make it different

explanation.surface: Police officers might make all the difference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but it means small coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose coins are called by this word, and to alter is to make something different.

clue.text: Sound off -—bawl out about scent knocked over

indicators.note: about means the scolding word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to rate someone is an old word for scolding them

indicators.note: knocked over suggests the scent word is tipped up and read backwards

parts.note: a nose is a smell or bouquet, as of wine

explanation.surface: Someone shouts and rails about a perfume bottle that was spilt.
explanation.walkthrough: To rate someone is an old word for scolding them; 'knocked over' gives ESON, and 'about' puts the scolding word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring out and echo is to sound loudly, so to sound off in a reverberating way.

clue.text: Steps taken by rebellious tot to find some weapon

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps over a fence

indicators.note: a rebellious tot will not stay in line, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A naughty toddler climbs some steps to find a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' are a stile over a fence, not dance moves; 'rebellious' gives TTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A slim dagger with a narrow blade is a kind of weapon.

clue.text: European in a minor dictator's service

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian serves under a petty tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan reads die-tater's for dictator's; the answer runs across minOR DICtator's.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian or other northern European is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Restricted allowance to a pound — so sensible

parts.note: a ration is a fixed limited allowance, as of food
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A limited payout of a pound is a prudent measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sensible means acting with reason and good judgement.

clue.text: Invests in most desirable seating

parts.note: the stalls are the best seats on the ground floor of a theatre

explanation.surface: A patron puts money into the best seats in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The STALLS are the ground-floor seats in a British theatre. 'Invests' means puts in office, not puts money in.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone is to place them formally in an office, as a bishop is put in post.

clue.text: An order resulting in military revolution

definitions.text: An order resulting in military revolution

parts.words: An order resulting in military revolution
parts.note: sounds like a command sparking a coup, but the revolution is soldiers turning round on parade

explanation.surface: A command triggers an army coup.
explanation.definitionFit: This drill command makes soldiers turn to face the opposite way.

clue.text: Maligned but greatly admired woman in top situation

indicators.note: in places the admired woman within the top

parts.note: a lid is the top of a container
a belle is a woman admired for her beauty

explanation.surface: A celebrated woman at the top was slandered anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top situation' is a lid, not a high position.
explanation.definitionFit: To be falsely defamed in print is to be slandered.

clue.text: Standing beside the head pastry-cook?

definitions.meaning: being at the side of something
the top tart-maker might be playfully crowned monarch of custard tarts

explanation.surface: Someone stands next to the chief baker.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as FLAN KING, the king of flans.
explanation.definitionFit: Positioned at the side of something, as troops guard a wing, and a whimsical title for a top baker.

clue.text: … a woman alone or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise asks for the letters arranged in a different way

explanation.surface: A woman by herself, or in some other state.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonora is a female given name, the heroine of Beethoven's Fidelio among others.

clue.text: A thief making little noise?

definitions.meaning: a stealer of cattle or horses
someone who makes soft crackling sounds, like leaves moving

explanation.surface: A burglar keeping quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle thief has this name, and so jokingly does anyone producing a soft swishing sound.

clue.text: What keeps a grandfather working

parts.note: suggests an elderly man staying employed, but the grandfather is a tall clock

explanation.surface: What stops an old man from retiring.
explanation.definitionFit: A swinging weight regulates a long-case clock, keeping it ticking.

clue.text: Change planes in Italy

indicators.note: change asks for the letters to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller switches flights in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges PLANES. The definition is 'in Italy': a city found there.
explanation.definitionFit: This port city stands on the southern Italian coast.

clue.text: The doctor uses new creamy concoction

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh word

explanation.surface: A physician uses a fresh creamy mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: MO (medical officer) is a crossword staple for doctor; 'new' gives USSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A light whipped dessert or creamy savoury dish fits a creamy concoction.

clue.text: Few will accept a large number in running water

indicators.note: accept means take in, so the first word holds the second

parts.note: a few is some
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Only a handful take in many in a flowing stream.
explanation.definitionFit: This river in northern France is flowing water, scene of a great First World War battle.

clue.text: There's little in copy to give rise to enthusiasm

indicators.note: in says the small word goes inside the copying word

parts.note: to ape is to copy or imitate
petit is French for little

explanation.surface: Imitation gives rise to only a little eagerness.
explanation.definitionFit: A keen desire or relish for something is a kind of eagerness.

clue.text: The standard set by an associate usually

parts.note: a norm is a standard or usual pattern
an ally is an associate or partner

explanation.surface: A partner usually sets the standard.
explanation.definitionFit: As a rule, in the ordinary course of things, means as usual.

clue.text: Supplying listening equipment, 'Edward's made !

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing
Ned is a pet form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Edward has made a living supplying hearing aids.
explanation.definitionFit: Money one has made by working is money gained in pay.

clue.text: The French sell with little hesitation, which is a bloomer

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
to vend is to sell
er is a small hesitant noise

explanation.surface: A French seller hesitates over a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This fragrant purple-flowered shrub is a plant that blooms.
